answer: Our admission window prices each new identity: the k-th admit in a 24 hour window posts k times a base bond, so a batch of 100 clones must escrow 5,050 base bonds instead of 100, and each bond stays locked to that one identity until it survives a random audit. A lagoon of free aliases becomes a river of real, per identity capital, and no squad can pool one pot across clones without losing it all at the first slashed audit. The kernel of the design is that cost grows quadratically with the number of fake identities, never linearly.
